key_insight: CatRetriever learns a shared latent space for slab and bulk crystals, turning slab-to-bulk catalyst discovery into a retrieval problem that can recover plausible parent bulk structures from generated surfaces.
engineering_relevance: This enables catalyst design workflows to move beyond surface-only generation and screen candidate bulks for synthesis-relevant properties like formation energy, symmetry, and adsorption-energy compatibility.
method: Contrastive representation learning aligns slab queries with corresponding bulk crystal representations.
A retrieval model ranks candidate parent bulks from a slab input in shared embedding space.
The framework is extended to a bulk discovery pipeline that combines retrieval, generative search expansion, and adsorption-energy distribution analysis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong retrieval performance with R@1 > 91% and R@3 > 98% on both in-distribution and holdout evaluation sets.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the slab and bulk candidate spaces are covered in training, so generalization to very novel catalyst chemistries or surface terminations should be validated carefully.
paper_title: CatRetriever: Contrastive Representation Learning for Slab-to-Bulk Retrieval in Generative Catalyst Discovery
